Hi Julia — great to meet you (virtually). We can support the Oct 26 window; first step is a scoping kickoff to validate traffic shape, model footprint, and networking/VPC constraints. Proposed slots: Tue 9/15 10:00 PT or Wed 9/16 14:00 PT — which works?

High-level thoughts (can refine after kickoff):
- Regions: US West (primary) + EU (secondary) is reasonable. We typically recommend colocating the bulk of steady capacity in the region with the largest user base and using cross-region fallback for EU traffic during failover.
- Initial sizing: ballpark 12–18 A100-class GPUs for steady traffic with burst capacity to ~32 for peak headroom depending on model tokenization and max seq length.
- Autoscale/burst policy: base pool + burst pool model. Example: base 16 GPUs (keep warm KV cache), burst to 32 with 2–3 minute scale window for step scaling on sustained traffic > 70% utilization. Fast-path scaling for sudden traffic spikes can be enabled but we recommend a controlled ramp for deterministic latency.
- Latency controls: prefix/KV caching for hot prompts, dynamic batch caps per route, and per-request priority routing for latency-SLA endpoints.

For kickoff, please share SOW/contract timeline and any procurement needs. I also attached a short pre-kickoff question checklist that helps us size the pool accurately.

Thanks — I looped in Monica (CS lead) and Marissa (implementation) to own the onboarding plan and runbook.

- Dylan

Thanks team — below is an initial implementation runway and checklist we will use for the kickoff. I'll own the implementation sprint and run the canary cutover.

Implementation Runway (high level)
- Week 0 (Discovery & Sizing): confirm model footprints (vocab, seq length), traffic segmentation, and SLA routes (owner: Monica)
- Week 1 (Provision & Network): provision base pool (16 GPUs) in US West, configure VPC peering, KMS keys, and audit log forwarding; prepare quantization profile if applicable (owner: Dylan + infra)
- Week 2 (Canary & Validation): deploy a canary in EU with 2–4 GPUs; run load tests and latency regression evals; validate autoscale triggers
- Week 3 (Rollout & Monitoring): enable burst to 32, start gradual traffic shift, enable cost-guardrails, and schedule weekly health checks

Preflight checklist (short)
- Procurement: signed SOW + PO; billing contact (procurement@stellar.ai)
- Network: VPC CIDR ranges, peering/VPN windows, ingress/egress rules, and NAT gateways
- Security: KMS key owner, rotation policy, SOC2 evidence requirements for logging retention
- Ops: on-call rotation for first 2 weeks of cutover, escalation policy, runbook links
- Observability: per-route dashboards, token-level cost slice, and alert thresholds for p50/p95 latency and error rates

Autoscale/burst policy proposal
- Base: 16 GPUs reserved (keep prefix cache warm)
- Burst policy: +50% cold capacity (to 24) with auto-burst up to 32 for sustained traffic >75% util for 3 minutes. Retract step at <50% util for 5 minutes.
- Cost controls: per-route rate limits and daily burn cap, alert on projected overspend >10%

Canary plan
- EU canary for 72 hours with synthetic traffic mirroring 10% of production; run latency/regression evals and compare output quality. If regressions > 2% or p95 exceeds 500ms, pause rollout.

Next steps for kickoff:
- Confirm kickoff time (Julia preferred Wed 9/16 14:00 PT)
- Customer to share final SOW draft and procurement timelines
- Soojin to share capacity_estimates by 9/17

Marissa Cole
Senior Implementation Manager, Redwood Inference
